column1: # Shared oracle (#1023 C), measured with the generated UBNF @f site (ParserGenerator's __CaptureSite: a
# LazyChain whose parseChainElement rejects a child Parsed that is not INPUT) at the low-level Classic entry,
# parse(context, kind, false), after a prefix of prefixCP code points of input "<prefix>c". Rust reads the same
# rows with Expr::Capture (`.capture("f")`) through parse_with_token_mode. Every row holds for Memoization x
# The field is the token of the site, which the mapper reads (its source text, and offsetFromRoot/length for
# typeofSpan): start/end are its raw offsets and text its text (~ for empty). In the virtual kinds the site
# LazyChain that collected nothing (zero width) is generated "", a detached source at raw 0-0 whatever the
# prefix; provenance shows it (Rust capture_spans has no provenance and is checked by span and text only).
# consumed/matched is the cursor after the parse; a rejection leaves it at the prefix with no field.
# rust is "=" when Rust agrees, else the Rust field: a known difference that existed before #1023 C. A custom
# child that publishes no Classic source (`leaf`, Expr::Custom) makes Rust's @f fall back to the cursor range,
# so in virtualTokenConsumed it is the cursor, while Java's site is generated "" at raw 0-0.
